body:
From Chris Bradley

I believe the following should really only for a "high value" applications, say Internet Banking:

2.25 Verify that the system can be configured to disallow the use of a configurable number of previous passwords.

2.31 Verify that if an application allows users to authenticate, they can authenticate using two-factor authentication or other strong authentication, or any similar scheme that provides protection against username + password disclosure.

comments.body:
Fixed in 3.1. We are not backing down on L2 and L3 apps *requiring* 2FA. The day of the password has passed. 

2.25 Verify that high value applications can be configured to disallow the use of a configurable number of previous passwords.

2.31 Verify that users can enrol and use TOTP verification, two-factor, biometric (Touch ID or similar), or equivalent multi-factor authentication mechanism that provides protection against single factor credential disclosure.

title: Consider re-wording or moving to L3
